A seismic attribute is a quantitative measure of a seismic characteristic of interest. It is derived from seismic data and used to interpret geologic structure, stratigraphy, and rock/pore fluid properties. Seismic attributes encompass all quantities derived from seismic data, including interval velocity, acoustic impedance inversion, pore pressure prediction, reflector terminations, complex-trace attributes, and amplitude variation with offset (AVO). 

Attributes can be classified into general and specific categories. General attributes are measures of geometric, kinematic, dynamic, or statistical features derived from seismic data, such as reflector amplitude, time, dip, azimuth, complex amplitude and frequency, coherence, and spectral decomposition. These are tied to lithology or geology and are broadly applicable. Specific attributes, however, have a less well-defined basis in physics or geology and may only correlate to geologic features in certain contexts.
